the Adolescent Coordinated Transitions (ACT) trial is a cluster randomized controlled trial that will compare a graduated transition and coordinated support group intervention against usual care in the transition of adolescents living with HIV (13-17 years) in Nigeria.
ACT is an intervention that aims to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity among ALHIV by improving their psychosocial wellbeing during transition from pediatric to adult HIV care.

ACT is a two-arm cluster RCT to evaluate the comparative effectiveness of the graduated transition and organized peer support intervention on retention, psychosocial wellbeing of adolescents living with HIV in resource-limited setting.
